for_senior_author: Risk of bias agreed (ROBINS-E, overall very high), with two remarks from the reader that are matters of judgment: (1) the study is in substance a prognostic-factor study, so if a claim ever cites the continuing-care or treatment-duration association as an intervention effect, ROBINS-I would be the apt instrument for that result; (2) the selection domain could defensibly be rated high for the descriptive relapse figures, since deaths and people not located (43% of sampled admissions) are plausibly related to continued use, although some concerns is within reason for the predictor associations.

Interpretation gap (judgment, unchanged) — missed item 1, verified in the source: Discussion ¶6 calls the hazard ratio of 0.93 per month 'a positive effect of longer index treatment duration'. Time in treatment is plausibly a marker of in-treatment response (36% used again in the first month after discharge or at discharge), so the association is confounded by response, and neither the confounding note nor the interpretation gap names this for the treatment-duration result.

Interpretation gap (judgment, unchanged) — missed item 2, verified in the source: Discussion ¶5 suggests that 3-to-5-year remission after methamphetamine treatment may not be substantially worse than for other drugs, although the study has no comparison group of people treated for other drugs and the comparison is informal, drawn from other published studies. Not noted in the interpretation gap.
